name: Eliud
overview: Eliud was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Achim within the genealogy of the Messiah. His mention is brief and specific, highlighting his place in the ancestral line leading to Christ. There are no additional notes recorded about his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliud appears once in Scripture without a given meaning or divine attribution. It is presented simply as a proper name within the genealogy recorded in Matthew 1:14.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Eliud as the son of Achim, and explicitly names Eleazar as his father in the following generation. Beyond these connections, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Eliud's significance lies in his role within the Messianic lineage, underscoring the human ancestry of Jesus Christ through the tribe of Judah. His mention in Matthew's genealogy serves to affirm the fulfillment of God's promise through a specific, traceable family line. Though not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion validates the historical and prophetic foundation of Christ's earthly heritage.
